To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ENIGMA is a new biclustering method that addresses the specific issues that are relevant for perturbational compundia and outperforms other existing methods on artificial datasets.
ENIGMA is an algorithm that extracts expression modules from perturbation compendia and that ENIGMA can be used to extract expression modules with internal substructures.

ENIGMA is a novel method to identify modules of coexpressed genes from perturbational expression profiles, and that ENIGMA modules are characterized by internal substructure and are less redundant than those produced by other methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational methods that can help to extract the maximum information from perturbational expression datasets.
the identification of gene expression modules from perturbation data.
the identification of coexpression patterns from perturbational expression profiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ENIGMA method constitutes a valuable addition in the repertoire of methods for analyzing perturbation gene expression data, and that the method is able to extract biologically relevant information from these compendia.
ENIGMA is a very useful tool to analyze expression data from perturbation experiments.
ENIGMA can be used as an alternative to other clustering methods for the analysis of perturbational gene-expression compendia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ENIGMA extracts biologically meaningful and non-redundant modules from perturbations of gene expression profiles.
the ENIGMA modules are more coherent and biologically meaningful than those generated by other biclustering methods.
ENIGMA can be seen as a novel, efficient and effective method for extracting expression modules from perturbation data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of differential expression analysis and biclustering can lead to the discovery of biologically meaningful expression modules.

the identification of overlapping expression modules, which are not redundant, is an essential step in the analysis of perturbational gene-expression compendia, and that this is best achieved by combining differential expression and clustering analysis.

the analysis of perturbational gene profiles should not be restricted to the identification of different sets of differentially expressed gene sets, but should also take into account their expression patterns.
